name: Red Rocks
summary: In northeastern Mulgore, the honored dead rest at Red Rocks. Young braves climb there to honor their ancestors and seek their wisdom.

sections.title: Hallowed Stones and Ancestral Graves
sections.body:
Red Rocks rises over northeastern Mulgore, its red stone marking sacred ground for the tauren. The most valiant dead lie here beside their forebears. Among them are chieftains, defenders, and champions who gave their lives to found and protect Thunder Bluff.

Young tauren come to these graves as part of their rites of passage. They honor the dead and listen for wisdom on the wind.

sections.title: The Quilboar Desecration
sections.body:
Bristleback quilboar have broken the peace at Red Rocks. They came from their dens and now infest the sandstone ledges, defiling ancestral graves with filth. For the tauren of Thunder Bluff, this desecration wounds their spiritual traditions.

Shaman and lorekeepers call for aid to cleanse the crags, drive out the Bristlebacks, and restore the resting place of their dead.

faq.q: What is the purpose of Red Rocks?
faq.answer: Red Rocks is the resting place of the most valiant fallen tauren. Young tauren also come to honor the dead as part of their rites of passage.

faq.q: Why are there quilboar at Red Rocks?
faq.answer: Bristleback quilboar came from their bramble burrows and overran the plateau, defiling the burial mounds. The tauren see this as an intolerable sacrilege against their ancestors' resting spirits.

faq.q: Who is buried at Red Rocks?
faq.answer: The most valiant tauren lie at Red Rocks. Among them are warriors who fought beside Cairne Bloodhoof to secure Mulgore and build Thunder Bluff, and heroes who died serving their tribes.
Tauren lay honored heroes to rest at Red Rocks, and braves come for the Rite of Wisdom. They leave offerings and listen for guidance from ancestral spirits on the wind.

angles.text: As a tauren, you know Red Rocks as sacred soil. Quilboar rooting among your honored ancestors' graves is an outrage that calls for cleansing.
As a shaman, you hear the sorrow of spirits disturbed by the quilboar's defilement. Your rites can restore elemental balance and peace for the ancestors.
